chunks: Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
Whoever dies and has no heir from kinship, nor a master of emancipation who has guaranteed his liability, then his wealth is from the anfal.

key_terms.الْأَنْفَالِ: property belonging to the anfal, under Islamic public authority
key_terms.جَرِيرَتَهُ: his liability or indemnified offense obligation in the legal sense
key_terms.مَوْلَى عَتَاقَةٍ: a patron connected through manumission of a slave

ai.seo_question: What happens in Shia fiqh to the wealth of someone who dies without any heirs?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the estate of a person who dies without any inheriting relative and without a wala' relationship of emancipation tied to guaranteed liability. In such a case, the deceased’s property is assigned to the anfal, placing it under the category of property administered by legitimate Islamic authority.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5714 - Al-Alaa narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said:
"Whoever dies and has no heir from relatives nor a freed slave who has guaranteed his liability (jarirah), then his wealth belongs to the anfal (public treasury or property of the Islamic state)."
